report.scope: Original 2017 standard core on balanced boards; normal Blight, solo and stated introductory alternatives. Expansions/promos, adversaries/scenarios, thematic maps and optional difficulty/scoring excluded.

limits: A broad initial filename enumeration returned unrelated paths and was truncated; no unrelated file contents were opened. It is not a text-input read and contributes no evidence.
References to prior reviews, histories and audits appearing inside allowed current files were read as part of those allowed files but never followed.

The reported compact old claims are the complete literal claims supplied in proposals.json. Their separate external compact-map occurrence was not inspected because that file is outside allowed inputs.

No claim that all possible original-card combinations were catalogued; unsupported producers remain unverified rather than declared impossible. This is complete-set adjudication, not whole-corpus saturation.

proposed_question_answer_fact_object.question: Bringer uses Spirits May Yet Dream to turn an unearned Fear Card in the Fear deck face-up. Does turning it face-up immediately earn that card or let players resolve its Fear effect now, or must it still be earned and resolved normally?

predetermined_answer.answer: Turning it face-up only previews the card. It does not earn it or resolve its effect. The card is still earned and resolved normally, with its Fear effect waiting for the ordinary Fear resolution procedure after it is earned.
minimum_asked_facts: Turning the card face-up does not itself earn the card.
Turning it face-up does not resolve its Fear effect or grant early resolution; normal earning and resolution still apply.
no_extra_grading_requirements: No arbitrary Fear-marker count, card identity, deck depth, threshold numerical recall, or complete Fear-step recital is required.
Do not require restating current Terror rules or a victory check not asked.

gap_decisions.independent_source_conclusion: The printed parenthetical defines the boundary of an original innate information permission: turn the face-down card face-up while retaining ordinary earning and resolution. The permission does not move a card into the earned area or activate its text. This explicit visibility-versus-status/timing branch is distinct from selection-location eligibility.

base_reachability.producer: Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares, Spirits May Yet Dream first threshold on original front panel.
witness: Original CORE p19 independently names Bringer in ordinary Repeat rules; native front/back and physical printed photo identity match.

Original setup includes unearned Fear Cards. Bringer can use the innate Fast with 2 Moon 2 Air. Uncovered original Air/Moon tracks plus the native Dread Apparitions Moon/Air provide a concrete original-component threshold witness; sufficient Growth turns and retained cards are ordinary states.
No adversary, scenario, extra trigger, expansion or new modifier is required. Solo also allows the ANY-Spirit target.

actual_ask_overlap_analysis.literal_question: Can Spirits May Yet Dream flip a Fear Card already earned, on top of the deck or deeper in the deck?
genuinely_required_facts: Spirits May Yet Dream's first effect may flip already-earned Fear cards, the top of the Fear deck, or deeper Fear cards.
actual_ask_overlap_analysis.assessment: Only asks whether flipping is permitted for three locations. A correct yes for every location does not assert whether the card has been earned or its effect resolves. Key and sole required fact likewise test location eligibility only.

actual_ask_overlap_analysis.literal_question: In a two-Spirit game with 7 of 8 Fear markers already generated, an effect generates 3 Fear and earning a card exposes Terror II. Explain marker handling, new Terror timing, and when the card is revealed/resolved.
genuinely_required_facts: The eighth Fear marker earns the top Fear card face-down, then reset all 8 markers to the Fear Pool.
The remaining 2 generated Fear go toward the next card.
Exposed Terror II takes effect immediately.
Reveal the earned card only as it is resolved during the Invader Phase's Fear step.
actual_ask_overlap_analysis.assessment: Asks marker 7-of-8 plus 3 Fear handling, immediate Terror II, and ordinary earned-card reveal/resolution timing. It has no preview intervention or question about whether visibility changes earning. The source-specific preview boundary can be misunderstood while this ordinary case is answered correctly.

actual_ask_overlap_analysis.literal_question: Three Fear Cards were earned in a known order. During the Fear step, may players inspect all three before resolving the first? In which order are they resolved, and where does each card go once resolved?
genuinely_required_facts: Do not inspect all earned Fear Cards before resolving the first; reveal/read them one at a time without looking ahead.
Resolve the initial earned stack in the order the cards were earned.
After resolving a Fear Card, put it in the Fear Discard space.
actual_ask_overlap_analysis.assessment: Asks ordinary already-earned stack inspection, earned order and discard. It tests no-look-ahead default; it does not ask what the explicit innate exception changes or preserves. Preserve all three existing requirements without construing the generic default as a ban on Bringer preview.

actual_ask_overlap_analysis.literal_question: When Spirits May Yet Dream grants its target an Element, may that Spirit choose an Element it currently has none of, or must the chosen Element already be present?
genuinely_required_facts: The granted Element must be a type the target already has at least one of; an absent Element cannot be chosen.
actual_ask_overlap_analysis.assessment: Asks the separate Element-grant instruction and existing-Element eligibility, not the first threshold’s Fear-card procedure.

actual_ask_overlap_analysis.literal_question: A Fear card resolved in the Fear step earns another Fear card and exposes a higher Terror Level. When is that new card resolved, at which level do subsequent cards resolve, and do “each player” choices require that player’s own Presence?
genuinely_required_facts: Put a newly earned Fear card at the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve it in the same Fear step.
Subsequent cards resolve only at the newly current Terror Level.
Each-player choices have no default requirement for that player's own Presence or Range; obey the card's restrictions.
actual_ask_overlap_analysis.assessment: New card earned during the Fear step and new Terror timing are ordinary earning/resolution questions, not effects of previewing an unearned card.

actual_ask_overlap_analysis.literal_question: After Invader cards advance, can Slow Powers remove a newly added Explorer to prevent a future Build, or has it already Built? When does Fear from a Slow Power normally resolve?
genuinely_required_facts: The just-added Explorer has only Explored; the card is in Build for next turn.
A Slow Power may remove it before then and thereby prevent a future Build if no Invaders remain.
Fear cards earned in Slow normally resolve in the next Invader Phase's Fear step.
actual_ask_overlap_analysis.assessment: Slow-generated Fear normally waits for the next Fear step; no innate preview or change to earned status is asked.

actual_ask_overlap_analysis.literal_question: State all four Terror victory conditions, the three standard defeat routes, and the result when a single Ravage loses a Spirit’s last Presence but surviving Dahan remove the final required Invader. Do you finish other lands first?
genuinely_required_facts: Terror I needs no Invaders; II no Towns/Cities; III no Cities.
Earning the final Fear card exposes Victory and wins without resolving its text.
Standard defeat routes are exhausted Blight as instructed, any Spirit without island Presence, and needing to draw from an empty Invader deck.
Finish the single-land Ravage and its triggered actions before checking outcomes.
If that tree meets both win and loss conditions it is a sacrifice victory.
Do not finish later land Ravages before checking.
actual_ask_overlap_analysis.assessment: Asks final-card Victory and defeat/action-tree procedure, not whether turning an unearned Fear Card face-up earns it.

gap_decisions.novelty_reasoning: The two facts are explicitly printed procedural limits of a special early-information permission. None of the 172 current stems requests whether using this preview earns the card or advances its resolution. Generic ordinary Fear timing does not test that a visibility exception preserves status and timing; an answer can satisfy Q87, Q11, Q139 and Q168 without resolving this branch. This is not a new numeric payload, target, name swap, ordinary arithmetic or arbitrary combination.
gap_decisions.grading_boundary: Require only the two proposed minimum facts, with equivalent wording accepted. Do not require Fear counts, card/deck position, threshold recall, complete Fear-step recital, Terror-level text or victory checks. Do not silently add these facts to Q87 or narrow its existing location permission.

classification_decisions.original_claim_effect: UNDERSTATES actual tested core scope by excluding the whole Optional timeboxing passage despite Q172.
classification_decisions.actual_question: Under The Urgency of War, is setting a limit on the time available to complete the Spirit Phase reserved for the game owner/organizer, or may any player set such a limit?
classification_decisions.approved_replacement_text: CORE p8 The Urgency of War contains an explicit optional ordinary-core permission: any player may limit the time available to complete the Spirit Phase. Q172 tests who may exercise that permission. Scope: original-core optional actor permission; question_ids: [Q172]. Timer/condition examples, particular durations, cooperative advice and any unprinted expiry consequences are not additional tested facts. This is not an excluded optional difficulty/scoring module.

tested_facts: Any player may set that Spirit Phase time limit; it is not reserved for the owner/organizer.

classification_decisions.reasoning: The original rulebook itself identifies a permitted actor and action attached to the ordinary Spirit Phase. It needs no Power producer. Optional exercise of an ordinary printed permission is not equivalent to an optional difficulty module. Who Decides applies when the actor is unspecified, so its owner/organizer fallback does not override the explicit any-player sentence. Q55 tests that general fallback, while Q172 directly tests this specific permission. The working scope row already classifies Q172 as supported; the compact exclusion should be reconciled.

approved_predetermined_answer.answer: Any player may set a limit on the time available to complete the Spirit Phase; it is not reserved for the game owner/organizer.

classification_decisions.original_claim_effect: OVERSTATES verified original-core reachability if the stipulated simultaneous producer is treated as established by its explicit-given wording.
classification_decisions.actual_question: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose? Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?
classification_decisions.approved_replacement_text: Q116 retains two fully graded branches. Given one simultaneous addition of two Blight to the stated land, each of the two Spirits loses one Presence there. Given two separate completed one-Blight additions, each loses Presence twice, totaling two disks per Spirit if still present. The simultaneous two-Blight producer is unverified in the assigned original core and receives zero current-base novelty credit; merely stipulating it does not verify it. The separate-additions branch is original-core supported, for example through a legal Powerstorm Repeat of Poisoned Land. Neither a cascade nor two separate uses proves simultaneity. Preserve all current question values, conditions, answer facts and regression grading.

simultaneous_addition.conditional_answer: One Presence per Spirit in the stated land.

two_separate_completed_additions.answer: Presence destroyed twice, two disks per Spirit if still present.

classification_decisions.reasoning: The full FAQ says each time one or more Blight is added to a given land, destroy one Presence of every Spirit there. That supplies the conditional result, not the original source of a two-at-once instruction. The FAQ multi-Blight example names Sweden, which is an excluded adversary. The standard Ravage rule adds only one regardless of damage; cascades are further additions to adjacent lands. Poisoned Land plus Repeat positively supports separate additions, not simultaneity. Current core-scope-credit already maintains exactly this split, so correct the compact claim without changing that working split.

approved_question.question: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose? Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?

approved_predetermined_answer.answer: The simultaneous addition destroys one Presence from each Spirit, even though two Blight tokens are added. Two separate additions destroy one Presence per Spirit on each addition, hence two per Spirit if available. Cascades elsewhere are outside the requested count.

approved_requested_clauses.actual_requested_clause: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose? Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?
required_facts: One simultaneous addition of two Blight destroys one Presence per Spirit in that land.
Two separate completed additions destroy Presence twice, totaling two disks per Spirit if still present.

classification_decisions.base_reachability_limits: No primary original-core simultaneous two-Blight producer was established in the inspected allowed evidence. This is not proof that none exists. Counting remains confined to the given land by the specified addition; no invented cascade totals or extra actors/costs are graded.

classification_decisions.original_claim_effect: OVERSTATES verified original-core reachability by treating the stipulated second card as producer proof.
classification_decisions.actual_question: Assume two Ravage Cards will be resolved in sequence. A land matching the second card is empty when the Ravage step begins, but a triggered effect during the first card moves an Invader there before the second card begins. Does that land Ravage from the second card, or was eligibility locked for the whole step?
classification_decisions.approved_replacement_text: Q142 is a source-correct, fully graded conditional engine regression: with the stipulated two Ravage Cards, determine a fresh affected-land list immediately before each card. The newly occupied land matching the second card Ravages from that card; the first card’s list does not lock eligibility for the whole step. A primary original-core producer of the second Ravage Card has not been verified, so both two-card clauses receive zero current-base novelty credit pending such proof. Preserve the complete current question, both required answer facts and all stated timing/trigger conditions.

actual_overlap_analysis.literal_question: A Stage III Ravage lists Sands and Jungles. Before it starts one matching land is empty. A triggered effect during another Ravage moves an Invader into that empty land and more Invaders into a land already due to Ravage. Which lands Ravage and which Invaders participate?
actual_overlap_analysis.assessment: Tests one card’s fixed affected-land list and new Invaders in an already eligible land. It is the nearest supported single-card procedure, but does not manufacture a second card or make Q142’s conditional two-card answer false.

actual_overlap_analysis.literal_question: After Explore, where do the Invader cards go? How are a Stage III two-terrain card and a Stage II flag handled without an Adversary?
actual_overlap_analysis.assessment: Asks ordinary single-card advancement. Stage III two terrains is one card, so it is not proof of the two-card premise.

classification_decisions.reasoning: The complete FAQ explicitly distinguishes the current card’s frozen list from a later Ravage Card, and its concrete additional-card example comes from Russia Level 5. That example is excluded here. Normal setup and advancement furnish one card in each ordinary action space, not the extra card. A triggered movement during the first card can be legitimate conditional engine context, but stipulating it and a second card does not establish an original producer of that second card. The working scope already assigns zero novelty, so the compact claim must agree.

approved_question.question: Assume two Ravage Cards will be resolved in sequence. A land matching the second card is empty when the Ravage step begins, but a triggered effect during the first card moves an Invader there before the second card begins. Does that land Ravage from the second card, or was eligibility locked for the whole step?

approved_predetermined_answer.answer: It Ravages from the second matching card. Each card determines its own affected-land list immediately before resolving that card; the first card’s fixed list does not lock eligibility for later cards.

report.overall_result: One distinct original-core preview/status-timing gap survives unchanged. All three compact classification corrections are approved with exact replacement text below. This is not a whole-corpus stopping PASS.

observations: Complete native panel inspected. Printed Bringer title, original art, Growth, both Presence tracks, special rule and both Innates are visible. No Aspect/exploratory overlay used.

Spirits May Yet Dream first threshold is 2 Moon 2 Air, Fast, targeting ANY Spirit; it flips a face-down Fear Card and expressly retains normal earning/resolution. Its separate 3-Moon threshold grants an Element the target already has.

Original upper Energy track: 2, Air, 3, Moon, 4, Any, 5. Lower Card Plays track: 2, 2, 2, 3, 3, Any. Uncovering Air and Moon plus Dread Apparitions supplies the first threshold using original components.
Other innate Night Terrors supplies Fear; it does not add a Fear-earning or early-resolution permission to the preview instruction.

relevant_regions.label: Complete Spirits May Yet Dream heading, attribute bar and both thresholds
Complete To Dream a Thousand Deaths and notes

transcriptions.text: Spirits May Yet Dream. Fast; ANY Spirit. 2 Moon 2 Air: Turn any face-down Fear Card face-up. (It’s earned/resolved normally, but players can see what’s coming.) 3 Moon: Target Spirit gains an Element they have at least 1 of.

To Dream a Thousand Deaths. Your Powers never cause Damage, nor can they Destroy anything other than your own Presence. When a Power of yours would Destroy (or deal enough Damage to Destroy) Explorer/Town/City, generate 0/2/5 Fear instead. The Power Pushes all Explorers/Towns it would Destroy. Notes: A single Power cannot Destroy a given Invader more than once. Powers which cause Damage via Dahan are affected just like all others. All effects other than Damage/Destroy work as usual.

Growth (Pick One): Reclaim Cards and Gain Power Card; Reclaim One and Add a Presence Range 0; Gain Power Card and Add a Presence Range 1; Add a Presence Range 4 to Land with Dahan or Invaders and Gain 2 Energy.
Night Terrors. Fast; Range 0; target land INVADERS. 1 Moon 1 Air: 1 Fear. 2 Moon 1 Air 1 Animal: +1 Fear. 3 Moon 2 Air 1 Animal: +1 Fear.

observations: Complete native back inspected; title and same artwork corroborate the front. Printed setup places 2 Presence in highest-numbered Sands on starting board. High complexity and a descriptive play-style paragraph accompany it.
The historical play-style statement about real offense is descriptive; current CORE/FAQ, including indirect destruction, governs rules. It is not used to extend or narrow the preview procedure.

transcriptions.text: Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares. SETUP: Put 2 Presence on your starting board in the highest-numbered Sands. COMPLEXITY: HIGH.

observations: Full original 2000x1181 photograph inspected. Bringer is the bottom panel of the middle column; art, title, Growth, original tracks and both Innate headings match the full native front.
Only left/middle original-eight group used. Right-column expansion/promo panels are outside assignment. Community caption/date are provenance/locators, not the substantive identity authority.
The photo cannot support every tiny printed word. Exact rules are read from the full native panel, and original CORE p19 independently names Bringer.

Whole original captured printed card face inspected, including all corners and Elements. It prints Moon and Air, supplies a normal original-Bringer threshold witness with track Air/Moon, and contains no preview earning/resolution exception.

transcriptions.text: Dread Apparitions. Cost 2; Fast; Range 1; target INVADERS. Printed Elements: Moon, Air. When Powers generate Fear in target land, Defend 1 per Fear. (Fear from To Dream a Thousand Deaths counts. Fear from destroying Town/City does not.)

observations: Whole original printed face inspected, including all corners. It adds exactly 1 Blight, not two simultaneous Blight. It supplies the separate-addition witness when legally Repeated.

transcriptions.text: Poisoned Land. Cost 3; Slow; Range 1; target ANY. Printed Elements: Earth, Plant, Animal. 1 Fear. 7 Damage. Add 1 Blight and destroy all Dahan. Threshold 3 Earth 2 Plant 2 Animal: For each Blight then present, +1 Fear and +4 Damage.

observations: Whole original printed face inspected, including all corners. Repeat is another use, not a single simultaneous two-Blight addition. With sufficient Energy it can Repeat Poisoned Land for the separate-instructions branch of Q116.

transcriptions.text: Powerstorm. Cost 3; Fast; target ANY Spirit. Printed Elements: Sun, Fire, Air. Target Spirit gains 3 Energy. Once this turn, target may Repeat a Power Card by paying its cost again. Threshold 2 Sun 2 Fire 3 Air: Target may Repeat up to 2 more Power Cards by paying their costs.
